nodes.text: Mind the pass, the soup goes through at speed. You are welcome in my kitchens, traveler, provided you stand somewhere the work is not.

choices.text: How do you feed a castle up a mountain?
What are the King and Queen like to serve?
Signy at the cookhouse says her kitchen feeds the real city.
I'll leave you to the proving.

nodes.text: Grain up the High Road from Amberford, greens off the Greenstair, fish out of two waters, salt when Saltmere's carts feel brave. Four hundred meals a week from five hearths. A castle is not a fortress, traveler. It is a list, and I keep it. The fortress part is what happens if I stop.

The King eats what the garrison eats and notices if it is better. The Queen reads my ledger for sport and has found one error in six years. I leave her one small one a month now, seeded fair. She knows. She finds it anyway, and writes SEEN beside it in a hand like a knife.

She is entirely right and I will deny saying so. Signy feeds two districts on shift bells with no ceremony to hide behind. I feed one castle that would eat ceremony if I let it. When her stores run short mine walk down the stair after dark, and no ledger of mine records the walk.
Safe roads. Eat before the climb down, it is longer than it looks.
